primary_diagnosis: Unstable Angina Pectoris with Multivessel Ischemia

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Recurrent retrosternal tightness triggered by walking stairs. Mild shortness of breath.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Aspirin 100mg daily, Clopidogrel 75mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg nightly.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Angina frequency diminished. Renal function rechecked: creatinine 1.5 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Added Bisoprolol 5mg OD. Withheld high-dose ARB until coronary angiogram review.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Valsartan (temporarily withheld due to border renal markers pre-cath)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Patient presented with intermediate risk unstable angina on diabetic background. Dual antiplatelet therapy combined with beta blockade successfully stabilized coronary perfusion without kidney compromise.

primary_diagnosis: Unstable Angina Pectoris with Borderline Renal Function

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Squeezing substernal chest discomfort radiating to left shoulder on moderate walking.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Administered Aspirin 100mg daily, Rosuvastatin 20mg nightly, Isosorbide dinitrate 10mg TID.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Angina frequency reduced by 80%. Blood pressure settling.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Atenolol 25mg OD with close monitoring of heart rate and renal labs.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Lisinopril (withheld due to baseline creatinine 1.8 and eGFR 39)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Patient has comorbid diabetic nephropathy and unstable angina. RAAS inhibitors held to avoid acute tubular injury. Medical optimization achieved with cardioselective beta blocker, statin, and organic nitrates.

primary_diagnosis: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Exertional dyspnea, elevated jugular venous pressure, normal systolic ejection fraction (60%).
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Started Empagliflozin 10mg daily, Chlorthalidone 25mg daily, Spironolactone 12.5mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: JVP decreased to normal, exertional capacity improved, weight down 3kg.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Confirmed normal serum potassium (4.7 mEq/L), continued SGLT2i and low dose MRA.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Verapamil (avoided due to bradycardia interaction)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Diastolic dysfunction with elevated filling pressures. EMPEROR-Preserved compliant regimen using SGLT2 inhibitor combined with low dose aldosterone antagonism resolved pulmonary congestion.

primary_diagnosis: Atrial Fibrillation with High Stroke Risk (CHA2DS2-VASc = 5)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Palpitations and anxiety, irregular pulse. Creatinine clearance calculated at 32 mL/min.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Apixaban 2.5mg BID (dose reduction criterion met for age >=80 or Cr >=1.5), Metoprolol 50mg OD.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Heart rate well controlled at 68 bpm. No bleeding manifestations or bruises.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued safe oral anticoagulation with renal safeguard.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Warfarin (previous hemorrhagic complication)
Dabigatran (avoided in low clearance)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Atrial fibrillation in stroke survivor with compromised renal reserve. Successfully anticoagulated with dose-reduced Factor Xa inhibitor.

primary_diagnosis: Post-PCI In-Stent Restenosis Investigation

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Exertional angina 9 months after right coronary artery bare-metal stenting.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Prasugrel 10mg daily + Aspirin 81mg, scheduled drug-coated balloon intervention.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Successful DCB angioplasty. Chest discomfort fully resolved.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained dual antiplatelet therapy for 6 months.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Ticagrelor (withheld due to patient non-adherence to twice-daily schedule)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: In-stent restenosis treated with paclitaxel-coated balloon. Potent once-daily P2Y12 inhibitor selected for optimized compliance.

primary_diagnosis: Severe Aortic Stenosis with Angina Symptoms

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Exertional lightheadedness, systolic ejection murmur radiating to carotids. Mean gradient 48 mmHg.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Avoided vasodilators, referred for Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR).

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Post-TAVR valve area 1.9 cm2. No heart block or paravalvular leak. Ambulating easily.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Single antiplatelet Aspirin 81mg daily.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Nitroglycerin (strictly contraindicated in severe aortic stenosis due to syncope risk)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Critical aortic valve stenosis successfully replaced via transfemoral catheter approach. Vasodilators strictly avoided pre-procedure.

primary_diagnosis: Premature Coronary Artery Disease with Elevated Lipoprotein(a)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Angina on vigorous jogging. Lp(a) elevated at 185 nmol/L, LDL-C 142 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Evolocumab 140mg SC every 2 weeks, Atorvastatin 80mg daily, Ezetimibe 10mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: LDL-C dropped to 32 mg/dL. Exertional stamina improved without chest symptoms.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained PCSK9 inhibitor triple therapy.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Niacin (not recommended due to flushing and lack of trial benefit)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Aggressive atherogenic lipid phenotype managed with monoclonal antibody PCSK9 inhibitor, achieving sub-40 LDL-C target.

primary_diagnosis: Diabetic Kidney Disease Stage 3b with Albuminuria

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Mild ankle swelling, uACR 680 mg/g. eGFR 38 mL/min.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Dapagliflozin 10mg daily, Telmisartan 40mg daily with potassium checks.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Swelling resolved. Expected transient eGFR dip to 35 mL/min (hemodynamic stabilization).
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained Dapagliflozin as transient dip is non-injurious; verified potassium at 4.6 mEq/L.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Glyburide (severe prolonged hypoglycemia risk in renal decline)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Cardiorenal protection initiated per DAPA-CKD guideline criteria. Transient initial GFR drop recognized as intra-glomerular pressure relief rather than injury.

primary_diagnosis: IgA Nephropathy (Berger's Disease) with Persistent Proteinuria

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Episodic macroscopic hematuria after pharyngitis. Proteinuria 1.8 g/24h.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Targeted-release oral Budesonide (Nefecon) 16mg daily, Losartan 100mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Hematuria subsided. Proteinuria reduced to 0.6 g/24h.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued gut-directed mucosal corticosteroid regimen without systemic steroid side effects.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: High-dose systemic Prednisone (avoided due to adverse glycemic and infectious profile)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Mucosal immunity targeting in primary IgA nephropathy. Significant attenuation of proteinuria without systemic corticosteroid toxicity.

primary_diagnosis: Renal Artery Stenosis (Atherosclerotic) with Renovascular Hypertension

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Resistant hypertension on 3 agents. Abdominal bruit heard on left flank.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Amlodipine 10mg daily, Carvedilol 25mg BID. Renin-angiotensin blockers withheld pending Doppler.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Doppler confirms unilateral 75% left renal artery stenosis. Blood pressure controlled on non-RAAS regimen.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued medical therapy avoiding bilateral RAAS-mediated perfusion collapse.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: ACE inhibitors / ARBs (potential acute decline in filtration pressure across stenotic vessel)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Hemodynamically significant unilateral renovascular stenosis controlled safely using calcium antagonist and vasodilating beta blocker.

primary_diagnosis: Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) - Primary

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Heavy pedal edema, hypoalbuminemia 2.2 g/dL, proteinuria 5.1 g/day.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Cyclosporine 3.5 mg/kg/day in divided doses, Prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day, Atorvastatin 20mg.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Marked reduction in edema, urine protein dropped to 1.8 g/day. Cyclosporine trough level 130 ng/mL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained calcineurin inhibitor with bi-weekly trough monitoring.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Macrolide antibiotics (erythromycin drastically elevates cyclosporine toxicity)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Primary steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome treated with calcineurin inhibition achieving partial remission.

primary_diagnosis: CKD Anemia in Non-Dialysis Patient

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Lethargy, pallor, exertional dyspnea. Hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, Ferritin 85 ng/mL, TSAT 16%.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Darbepoetin alfa 25 mcg SC every 2 weeks, Ferric Carboxymaltose 500mg IV single dose.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Vitality substantially improved. Hemoglobin rose to 10.6 g/dL (within safe target 10-11.5 g/dL).
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained Darbepoetin interval, avoided targeting Hb > 11.5 to prevent stroke risk.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Iron Dextran (severe anaphylactic reaction)
Over-correction of Hb > 12 g/dL
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Renal anemia corrected safely under KDIGO hemoglobin threshold guidelines using long-acting erythropoietin analogue and non-dextran intravenous iron.

primary_diagnosis: Recurrent Calcium Oxalate Nephrolithiasis with Mild Renal Impairment

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Recurrent right renal colic, 24-hr urine calcium 380 mg/day (elevated).
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Indapamide 2.5mg daily (reduces urinary calcium excretion), Potassium Citrate 20 mEq BID.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: No flank pain episodes. 24-hr urine calcium reduced to 190 mg/day, urinary pH alkalized to 6.8.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained Indapamide and citrate therapy with high fluid intake.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: High-dose dietary calcium restriction (counter-intuitively increases oxalate absorption)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Metabolic stone prevention accomplished through thiazide-type hypocalciuric action and urinary alkalinization.

primary_diagnosis: Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis Late Presentation

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Periorbital edema, dark tea-colored urine following skin infection. ASO titer 640 IU/mL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Furosemide 40mg daily, Amlodipine 5mg daily, dietary sodium restriction.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Urine cleared of macroscopic blood, edema subsided, blood pressure normalized.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Tapered diuretic as spontaneous post-infectious healing progressed.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Corticosteroids (unwarranted in typical post-streptococcal disease)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Immune-complex mediated acute glomerulonephritis managed expectantly with volume decongestion and blood pressure support.

primary_diagnosis: Uncontrolled Type-2 Diabetes with Atherosclerotic CVD Risk

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Polydipsia, postprandial fatigue, HbA1c 9.2%, unable to take biguanides.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5mg weekly SC injection, Empagliflozin 25mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Fasting glucose down from 210 to 124 mg/dL. Weight down 2.8 kg. No GI intolerance.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained dual incretin/SGLT2 therapy with excellent cardiovascular protective coverage.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Metformin (intractable GI cramping)
Pioglitazone (avoided in vascular disease / heart failure risk)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Metformin-intolerant type-2 diabetes managed via combination GLP-1 RA and SGLT2i, achieving target glycemic control and ASCVD risk reduction.

primary_diagnosis: Hashimoto's Thyroiditis with Severe Symptomatic Hypothyroidism

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Severe fatigue, cold intolerance, constipated, facial myxedema. TSH 44 mIU/L, Free T4 0.4 ng/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Levothyroxine 100 mcg daily taken 60 minutes before breakfast with full glass of water.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Energy restored, heart rate normalized, constipation cleared. Repeat TSH 3.2 mIU/L.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Instructed to separate oral iron supplements from Levothyroxine by at least 4 hours.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Concurrent calcium/iron co-administration (blocks thyroxine absorption)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Overt primary autoimmune hypothyroidism restored to euthyroid status with pure sodium levothyroxine. Drug absorption interaction counseling reinforced.

primary_diagnosis: Primary Hyperparathyroidism with Symptomatic Hypercalcemia

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Lethargy, constipation, polyuria. Serum calcium 11.8 mg/dL, intact PTH 142 pg/mL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: IV 0.9% Saline rehydration 200 mL/h, Cinacalcet 30mg BID, Sestamibi SPECT scan arranged.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Serum calcium normalized to 9.8 mg/dL. SPECT scan showed solitary right inferior parathyroid adenoma.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Referred to endocrine surgery for minimally invasive parathyroidectomy.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Thiazide diuretics (contraindicated as they decrease urinary calcium excretion and worsen hypercalcemia)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Symptomatic primary hyperparathyroidism stabilized pharmacologically with calcimimetic Cinacalcet prior to definitive surgical cure.

primary_diagnosis: Type-2 Diabetes with Microalbuminuria and Hepatic Steatosis

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: ALT 68 U/L, AST 54 U/L, HbA1c 8.7%, uACR 180 mg/g.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Pioglitazone 30mg daily (benefits NASH fibrosis), Dapagliflozin 10mg daily.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Transaminases normalized (ALT 28, AST 24), fasting glucose down to 118 mg/dL.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued dual regimen, monitored weight and absence of pedal edema.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Pioglitazone in symptomatic heart failure (ruled out baseline cardiac failure)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Thiazolidinedione and SGLT2i combination demonstrated dual glycemic and hepatic histologic benefit in fatty liver disease with early nephropathy.

primary_diagnosis: Type-1 Diabetes Mellitus - Basal-Bolus Optimization

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Frequent nocturnal hypoglycemia and post-breakfast spikes. HbA1c 8.9%.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Transitioned to Insulin Degludec 18 units nightly, Insulin Aspart 1 unit per 10g carbohydrate with meals.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) time-in-range increased from 48% to 76%. Zero nocturnal hypos.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Maintained ultra-long-acting basal analogue and automated carb-ratio dosing.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Oral sulfonylureas (strictly ineffective and contraindicated in absolute insulin deficiency)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Type-1 diabetes stabilized using second-generation ultra-flat basal insulin profile, eliminating hypoglycemic unawareness.

primary_diagnosis: Acromegaly (Post-Transsphenoidal Resection Residual Disease)

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Coarse facial features, ring tightening, IGF-1 elevated at 2.4x upper limit of normal.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Initiated Octreotide LAR 20mg deep intragluteal injection monthly.

longitudinal_timeline.symptoms: Soft tissue swelling in fingers improved, headache relieved, IGF-1 dropped to 1.1x normal.
longitudinal_timeline.intervention: Continued monthly somatostatin receptor ligand with ultrasound monitoring of gallbladder.

adverse_or_contraindicated_drugs: Dopamine antagonists (metoclopramide avoided)
treatment_outcome.clinical_notes_raw: Persistent growth hormone hypersecretion following surgical adenomectomy successfully suppressed with long-acting somatostatin receptor analogue.
